findings.title: Endpoint observation is not bound to the same switch scope and mutation-free read step
counterexamples: Real endpoint Read E, add an interface without advancing time, Capture fresh switch scope B with same node count, then Read(E,B): existing checks accept stale endpoint coverage
Real endpoint Read E then enqueue at same nanosecond before switch Read: old queue values are copied because time equality is not a state freshness proof
findings.minimum_action: Share and validate complete scope provenance and enforce one mutation-free combined actual endpoint/switch read. Prefer a combined entry that performs actual endpoint Read immediately with switch read; alternatively use enforced provenance/state versions. Timestamp/context alone is insufficient.
findings.claim_boundary: Static conditional counterexamples only; no false drain or mask255 execution claimed

findings.title: Captured interface pointer slots omit actual owner/index/non-null/unique binding validation
findings.counterexample: Capture, change a switch device's public ifIndex without changing Node device vector; current Validate still accepts. A reparented/shared device is not independently excluded either.
findings.minimum_action: At Capture and Validate require non-null device, GetNode()==captured node and GetIfIndex()==slot; deduplicate over the full scope at Capture and preserve unique binding. Align allowed interface types with endpoint scope; do not repair bad objects during read.
findings.claim_boundary: Upstream endpoint validation may reject some bad shapes, but it does not establish this new scope's own binding contract

next: Repair composite scope/read and device bindings, then actual-switch fixture; no execution authority
